angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,112,837 km at 52.60 pc = 1.81 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13061: distance 52.604 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 52.604 +/- 0.579 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 19.0390 +/- 0.1262 mas (same row, RUWE 1.25), 150.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.224 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13061: radius 10.224 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 46.769 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,112,837 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4724 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13061: effective temperature 4724 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.08) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 13061: effective temperature 4724 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.08) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * 39 Ari: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * 39 Ari: projected rotation speed 4.5 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 17361) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.67 from 2023ApJS..266...41P; the 21 published values span log g 1.8 to 2.85, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.3% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...41P)
